images.caption: Abbeyleix Bog. Killamuck Bog is a special area of conservation and home to a variety of plant and animal species. You may encounter a range of mosses, sedges, and heathers, which thrive in the acidic soil of the bog. During the spring and summer months, colourful wildflowers, such as orchids and bog cotton, can also be spotted along the trail. The bog is an important habitat for insects, including dragonflies and butterflies, as well as amphibians like frogs and newts. Birds such as skylarks, meadow pipits, and snipe can be heard or seen throughout the year, while mammals like foxes and hares may also make an appearance.

images.caption: Abbeyleix Bog Boardwalk. In addition to its ecological significance, Killamuck Bog holds cultural importance, as boglands in Ireland have long been a source of fuel and a key part of rural life. Conservation work in the area focuses on preserving this unique habitat while raising awareness of its value to both nature and heritage. This walk provides an opportunity to learn more about these efforts while enjoying a peaceful and scenic environment.

description: This circular loop walk takes you around Killamuck Bog near the town of Abbeyleix in County Laois. The walk starts at the entrance near the Abbeyleix Manor Hotel. You can then follow boardwalks around the site. The trail provides an easy and accessible route through the bog, allowing visitors to experience the natural beauty of this important wetland habitat. Along the way, you will find a series of interpretive panels that provide insight into the history, ecology, and conservation efforts associated with the bog. The path is well-maintained and offers views of the surrounding countryside, creating a tranquil atmosphere for walkers. You can continue your walking in the area by heading north to visit the Rock Of Dunamase. Here you can explore the atmospheric ruins of a fascinating ancient Celtic fortification. Near here you can also pick up the epic Slieve Bloom Way .
